canonical_statement: Intravenous UFH was ordered through an EMR order set that included monitoring of heparin concentrations by anti-Xa assay.
Charts were reviewed manually in the EMR and data were recorded in REDCap to standardize data collection and reduce researcher variability.
One primary outcome was the incidence of new or worsening thrombus while patients were receiving intravenous UFH.

concept.text: New or worsening thrombus while receiving intravenous UFH

canonical_statement: One primary outcome was the incidence of bleeding while patients were receiving intravenous UFH; bleeding was categorized as major or minor using ISTH definitions.

outcome.definition: Bleeding was categorized as major or minor using ISTH-based definitions.

canonical_statement: Major bleeding was defined as fatal bleeding, bleeding involving a critical organ, bleeding causing a hemoglobin decline greater than 2 g/dL, or bleeding requiring red-blood-cell transfusion.

outcome.definition: Fatal bleeding; critical-organ bleeding (intraspinal, intracranial, retroperitoneal, or pericardial); >2 g/dL hemoglobin decline; or red-blood-cell transfusion requirement.

canonical_statement: One secondary outcome was transfusion requirement within 1 month of UFH initiation.
One secondary outcome was death within 3 months of UFH initiation.

Statistical analysis used descriptive statistics, Fisher exact testing for categorical comparisons, independent t testing or Wilcoxon rank-sum testing for numerical comparisons, and multivariable logistic regression built from univariate variables with p<0.05 using stepwise selection.
The study received University of Florida IRB approval under project IRB201702116 before data collection.

canonical_statement: The authors attributed the higher observed bleeding and transfusion rates in the LI group to selection of a higher-risk population for the low-intensity protocol.
The authors concluded that the similar incidence of new or worsening thrombosis suggests the LI protocol may have efficacy comparable to the SI protocol.

concept.text: New or worsening thrombus while receiving intravenous UFH

canonical_statement: The abstract states that target anti-Xa levels of 0.25-0.35 IU/mL may be more optimal in high-risk patients.

The authors interpreted the nearly identical HAS-BLED scores despite differences in bleeding history and bleeding incidence as evidence that HAS-BLED is not applicable for bleeding-risk determination in patients receiving UFH.
The study was retrospective and nonrandomized.

Protocol selection was based on clinician judgment, and the LI group had a higher baseline bleeding-risk profile, creating substantial confounding by indication when comparing bleeding outcomes between protocols.

The authors called for a prospective randomized trial matching comorbidities, risk factors, and indications to further evaluate the two protocols and support development of a UFH bleeding-risk stratification system and weight-based dosing nomogram.
